about.title: Richmond Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Richmond is a working city, and a lot of its 109,708 residents earn a living on job sites, in warehouses, on loading docks, or behind the wheel. When something goes wrong at work, the first system you meet is California workers' compensation. It covers medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who was at fault, and in most situations it is the only claim you can bring against your own employer. What many injured workers in Contra Costa County never hear is that a second path may exist. If a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective piece of equipment, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate personal injury claim against that third party. This matters for people who drive for work along I-80, Richmond Parkway, Barrett Avenue, or I-580, the corridors where public records logged the city's highest collision counts. We can review your situation at no cost. Our team can help you sort out which claims fit your situation.

items.title: We look past the workers' comp ceiling
items.desc: Workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it does not stop a claim against a negligent third party. Our team knows how to spot that second claim.

items.title: Deadlines handled early, not late
items.desc: You should report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party injury claim in California carries a two-year filing window. Acting quickly helps protect both.

items.title: Protection if your employer pushes back
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury is illegal in California. We can explain your rights if hours get cut or the job suddenly disappears after you file.

items.question: I was hit by another driver while making deliveries on Richmond Parkway. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation applies regardless of who caused the crash. Because another driver was involved, you may also have a separate personal injury claim against that driver, which can cover losses workers' comp does not, such as pain and suffering. We can help coordinate the two so they do not work against each other.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: Usually no. California law makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, even if the employer was careless. The exceptions are narrow, but claims against other parties, like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer, are not blocked by that rule.

items.question: How does your process work, and what does it cost?
items.answer: We offer a free initial review of your case. You tell us what happened, and our team can help you understand whether you have a third-party personal injury claim alongside workers' compensation. We handle Richmond and Contra Costa County matters on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and there is no obligation.
